title: P3 design RAG — token, replay and key-lifecycle foundations

sections.title: P3 design RAG — token, replay and key-lifecycle foundations
sections.text:
**Verified:** 2026-09-19  
**Boundary:** External sources constrain security properties and terminology. Agentools envelope
layout, class names, SQL identifiers, error codes and phase ownership are repository design
decisions (`RAG:—`), not claims sourced from IETF/NIST/PostgreSQL.

Perplexity was queried twice through the configured `plugin-core-perplexity` MCP: one
web+academic synthesis of RFC 8725 controls versus JWT-as-requirement, and one web synthesis of
PostgreSQL `ON CONFLICT` consume plus RFC 8259 duplicate names. Every load-bearing claim below
was then rechecked by fetching the linked primary source. Native WebFetch succeeded for
RFC 8725, RFC 8259, PostgreSQL `INSERT` and transaction isolation, and NIST SP 800-57 Pt 1 r5.

| Evidence | Verified claim | P3 consequence |
|:--|:--|:--|
| RAG:✅ [RFC 8725 §2.1](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8725.html#section-2.1), accessed 2026-09-19 | Libraries MUST let the caller specify a supported algorithm set and MUST NOT use any other; `alg`/`enc` MUST match the operation; each key MUST be used with exactly one algorithm. Unsigned `alg` in a JOSE header is the historical confusion vector, including `"none"`. | v1 allowlist is `HS256` only; `alg` is signed inside the payload and pinned to the key; `none` is not enabled. This does not adopt JWT. |
| RAG:✅ [RFC 8725 §2.1](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8725.html#section-2.1) `"none"` paragraph, accessed 2026-09-19 | `"none"` is acceptable only when another cryptographic layer already protects the JWT; libraries SHOULD NOT generate or consume `"none"` unless the caller explicitly asks. | Confirmation tokens are bearer application credentials, not TLS session tickets. `"none"` stays forbidden. |
| RAG:✅ [RFC 8725 §3.8](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8725.html#section-3.8), [§3.9](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8725.html#section-3.9), [§3.10](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8725.html#section-3.10), accessed 2026-09-19 | If `iss` is present, keys MUST belong to that issuer. If one issuer serves multiple relying parties, `aud` MUST be present and checked. `kid` is a lookup handle and must be sanitized; it is not a trust anchor. | Envelope carries `iss`/`aud`/`kid`; lookup is `(tenant, purpose, kid)` from the trusted provider, never from an attacker-supplied URL. |
| RAG:✅ [RFC 8725 §3.11](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8725.html#section-3.11), accessed 2026-09-19 | Different JWT kinds from one issuer need mutually exclusive validation (explicit type, distinct `aud`/`iss`, or equivalent). | `purpose` is a signed closed enum (`confirmation`); event/other tokens cannot verify as confirmation tokens. |
| RAG:✅ [RFC 8725 §3.5](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8725.html#section-3.5), accessed 2026-09-19 | Human-memorizable passwords MUST NOT be used directly as keyed-MAC keys such as HS256. | Key material is CSPRNG bytes ≥ 32; tests reject empty/short secrets. |
| RAG:✅ [RFC 8259 §4](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8259.html#section-4), accessed 2026-09-19 | Object names SHOULD be unique; duplicate names make receiver behavior unpredictable (last pair, error, or all pairs). The RFC does not say last-wins. | P3 parsers MUST reject duplicate names before interpreting claims. PHP `json_decode` / Dart `jsonDecode` are not a sufficient profile. |
| RAG:✅ [PostgreSQL INSERT — `ON CONFLICT` / `RETURNING`](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/sql-insert.html), accessed 2026-09-19 | `DO NOTHING` skips insert on arbiter conflict. `RETURNING` returns only rows actually inserted or updated. Unique indexes can block concurrent sessions on the same key. | Consume is `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (tenant_id, token_id) DO NOTHING RETURNING token_id`. Empty RETURNING is spent; do not treat it as “check then proceed”. |
| RAG:✅ [PostgreSQL transaction isolation — Read Committed `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/transaction-iso.html), accessed 2026-09-19 | In Read Committed, `DO NOTHING` may skip insert because of another transaction whose effects are not visible to the INSERT snapshot. `DO UPDATE` documents an atomic insert-or-update guarantee; `DO NOTHING` documents the skip. | Empty RETURNING is fail-closed “not the winner”. No SELECT-after-empty against a stale snapshot. `DO UPDATE` is not used as the consume primitive. |
| RAG:✅ [NIST SP 800-57 Part 1 Rev. 5 §7](https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/sp/800/57/pt1/r5/final), [glossary](https://nvlpubs.nist.gov/nistpubs/specialpublications/nist.sp.800-57pt1r5.pdf), accessed 2026-09-19 | Key states include Active (protect and/or process), Deactivated (no new protection, may still process), Compromised, Destroyed. Cryptoperiod is the authorized use span. | Map `active` → Active, `verify_only` → Deactivated/recipient-only, `compromised` → Compromised (reject), `retired` → Destroyed/not used. NIST does not prescribe Agentools class names or a cryptoperiod length. |

sections.title: Facts intentionally not promoted
sections.text:
- RFC 8725 is a JWT BCP. It does not require Agentools to emit JWS/JWT compact serialization.
- RFC 8725 `"none"` guidance is not a license to ship unsigned confirmation tokens.
- RFC 8259 duplicate-name language is SHOULD/unpredictable, not a MUST-reject for generic JSON;
  reject-duplicates is P3's application profile.
- PostgreSQL `ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE` atomicity wording is not a reason to upsert consume rows.
- NIST key states do not require an HSM, KMIP, AWS KMS, or a 1–2 year cryptoperiod for this package.
- Audit SQL sketches are not the schema; F14 already rejected them as norms.
